title: PHOSPHOR 0.2: pixel VFX you can make with your coding agent, no VFX experience needed. Here's what one prompt got me
author: sinopsky
selftext:
I'm not a VFX artist, and pixel effects were always the part of my games I put off. Fire that doesn't look like a traffic cone, water that actually flows, explosions with some weight to them.

So I built PHOSPHOR, a free pixel VFX editor, and in 0.2 I made it work well with agents. Every effect is a JSON scene, and the download comes with a skill file and command-line tools. The agent writes the scene, renders it, looks at the frames and tweaks it, and you steer it in plain words: less glow, teal fire, slower ash.

The video is one prompt in Claude Code. It took a few render passes, and it caught on its own that the burning text was blowing out under bloom.

When you like it, one export gives you a Godot .tres, a GameMaker strip and an .aseprite file. Everything stays editable in the browser editor too, if you'd rather tweak by hand.

Comment an effect you need for your game and I'll run it and reply with the gif to test it!

comments.author: sinopsky
comments.body:
"Create an pixel-art VFX scene in PHOSPHOR that shows off everything the engine gained recently, in ONE coherent shot: animated pixel text whose letters turn into matter, splines, speed/gravity/spin-over-life curves, bezier keyframe timing, the new fire behaviour, art-directable water and custom simulation colours. Pick a strong concept yourself."

tool + the skill file: [https://sinopskyd.itch.io/phosphor](https://sinopskyd.itch.io/phosphor)

comments.author: i_rate_slop
comments.body:
I think it's interesting to see trends in words with each new model release. I've had GPT try to name like 3 separate projects Phosphor and I've seen so many indie games called some variation of phosphor over the past half year.

Apologies if you named it phosphor on your own. Just an observation and it's not a problem, just an interesting trend.

https://i.redd.it/iwi4uhbs2pxh1.png

replies.author: sinopsky
replies.body: ha, fair. I picked it because of CRT phosphor, that trends chart is wild though

comments.author: Ok_Way1689
comments.body:
Can you share the prompt you used to create this video?

Any plans for an MCP? I assume it's a CLI at the moment that was invoked by your harness?

replies.author: sinopsky
replies.body:
Prompt's in my comment up top, it's basically "Create an pixel-art VFX scene in PHOSPHOR that shows off everything the engine gained recently, in ONE coherent shot: animated pixel text whose letters turn into matter, splines, speed/gravity/spin-over-life curves, bezier keyframe timing, the new fire behaviour, art-directable water and custom simulation colours. Pick a strong concept yourself."  
and yeah it's CLI right now, claude code just reads the skill file and calls the node scripts through bash  
  
MCP is planned for the next update. The idea is the server opens the editor in your browser and the agent edits the scene live, so you actually watch layers appear and can jump in and tweak stuff yourself mid-way

replies.author: gimdeka_studio
replies.body:
yeah still blows my mind till today 😂 

mind to share few cents of it?  
I'd like to research how it works, but don't know where to start with AI ahaha

replies.author: sinopsky
replies.body:
For sure. I was doing sims way before AI, mostly fluids and smoke in blender, so it's been a long rabbit hole lol. The easiest start: download PHOSPHOR, open the folder in any AI tool, and just ask anything. The whole engine is one readable index.html, so the AI can break it down piece by piece.  
Petri's Noita GDC talk is great background too! It explains this really clearly

comments.author: ShibaBandit
comments.body: Looks great, how is the performance hit in-game?

replies.author: sinopsky
replies.body: Basically zero 😆 the sim only runs in the editor. What goes into your game is a baked sprite sheet, so in-engine it's just an animated sprite flipping frames like any hand-drawn effect. The only cost is the texture, and at pixel sizes those are tiny. Tradeoff is it's not interactive at runtime, it plays the same every time
